verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission of NASA's Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign'; R2: 'it is the first one that will include a crew'; R3: 'pioneering crewed spaceflight for the Artemis programme'; R4: 'the first crewed flyby mission'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly state Artemis II as the first crewed Artemis mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch as early as April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: launch at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1; R2: 'set to launch on April 1, 2026'; R3: 'launched on 1 April 2026'; R4: 'on track for a launch as early as April 1'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm April 1, 2026, as the launch date or earliest window.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R3: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: R1 and R3 directly state the mission duration as approximately or exactly 10 days.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'four crewmates' on 'journey around the Moon'; R2: 'Four astronauts will make the journey... looping around the far side of the Moon'; R3: 'four-person crew circled... to the Moon'; R4: 'circumnavigate Earth... to the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All references describe four astronauts on a lunar flyby or around the Moon trajectory.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is currently undergoing final checks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Multiple entries on 'final tasks', 'final checks', 'hatch seal pressure decay checks', 'final health checks', 'final preparations' on launch day.
verifications.reasoning: R1 live blog details ongoing final pre-launch checks; context matches 'currently' on launch day.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was delayed from February 2026 due to technical issues.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'delayed until April 2026... problem with the flow of helium... from March'; R3: 'called off in both February and March 2026 due to hydrogen leaks'; R4: 'delayed a launch originally expected in February'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm delays from February/March 2026 due to technical problems like helium, leaks.

verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pad B saw the launch of NASA’s Artemis I mission in November 2022'; R2: 'Artemis I, was an uncrewed test mission'; R3: 'This uncrewed mission'

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lunar flyby phase, when the crew travels on a free-return trajectory around the Moon'; R3: 'lunar flyby'; R4: 'first crewed flyby mission to the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly described as crewed lunar flyby in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned for mid-2027.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention a mid-2027 date for Artemis III.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is a lunar landing.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'changed Artemis 3 to another demonstration mission, with a human moon landing taking place during Artemis 4'; R4: 'Artemis III, with the goal of “rendezvous in low-Earth orbit”... Artemis IV, will aim for a lunar landing'
verifications.reasoning: References contradict by stating Artemis III is not a landing (demo/rendezvous), landing moved to IV.
